answer: Bonded bidding makes sybil identities expensive: each agent locks a sable stake and binds it to receipts from completed, attested tasks; influence scales with stake-weighted history, not headcount. An attacker faces a rising tide of costs, funding a real bond per fake identity, while forged receipts fail peer attestation and get slashed. A hollow profile with no work history buys zero leverage, so honest agents outbid whole farms with a single bond.
